query: What is Section 1 of BNS about?

required_points: Provides the short title: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
Sets out the intra-territorial and extra-territorial application of the Sanhita.
optional_points: Mentions that different dates may be appointed for different provisions.
forbidden_points: Stating it applies only to certain states of India.
Confusing it with the procedural code (BNSS).

query: Explain Section 2 of BNS in simple words.

required_points: Section 2 is the definition clause containing statutory explanations for words used throughout the code.
optional_points: Words not defined here but defined in the IT Act or BNSS inherit meanings from there.
forbidden_points: Stating that Section 2 specifies substantive criminal punishments directly.

query: What punishments are listed under Section 4 of BNS?

required_points: Lists the specific punishments: death, imprisonment for life, imprisonment (rigorous or simple), forfeiture of property, fine, and community service.
optional_points: Identifies community service as a newly codified form of punishment.
forbidden_points: Including transportation for life or whipping as valid categories.

query: What does Section 6 say about life imprisonment and term calculation?

required_points: In calculating fractions of terms of punishment, imprisonment for life is reckoned as equivalent to imprisonment for twenty years.
optional_points: Notes that this mathematical rounding rule applies unless specific context dictates otherwise.
forbidden_points: Stating that all life sentences automatically terminate at twenty years.

query: Explain Section 14 of BNS.

gold_references.label: Act done by a person bound, or by mistake of fact believing himself bound, by law

required_points: Nothing is an offence which is done by a person who is, or who by reason of mistake of fact and not mistake of law in good faith believes himself, bound by law to do it.
optional_points: Mentions the statutory illustration of a soldier firing on a mob by order of his superior officer.
forbidden_points: Allowing a mistake of law to act as an excuse under this exception.

notes: Grounds the baseline general exception rule for bound acts.

query: What is the accident exception under Section 18?

gold_references.label: Act of accident in the doing of a lawful act

required_points: Nothing is an offence which is done by accident or misfortune.
The act must be done without any criminal intention or knowledge in the doing of a lawful act in a lawful manner by lawful means and with proper care and caution.
optional_points: The classic example involves a person working with a hatchet where the head flies off.
forbidden_points: Protecting an individual who is doing an illegal act or acting with complete negligence.

notes: Focuses on accident and misfortune conditions.

query: What does Section 20 say about children under seven years?

gold_references.label: Act of a child under seven years of age

required_points: Nothing is an offence which is done by a child under seven years of age.
This sets an absolute standard of doli incapax.
optional_points: No evidence can be admitted to show that the child possessed maturity to understand the crime.
forbidden_points: Allowing exceptions where a 6-year-old child can be sentenced to juvenile custody.

notes: Absolute legal bar on capacity based on age.

query: Explain Section 22 on unsoundness of mind.

gold_references.label: Act of a person of unsound mind

required_points: Nothing is an offence which is done by a person who, at the time of doing it, by reason of unsoundness of mind, is incapable of knowing the nature of the act, or that he is doing what is either wrong or contrary to law.
optional_points: The impairment must exist strictly at the precise moment the act is committed.
forbidden_points: Applying the exception to simple medical insanity without proof of legal cognitive incapacity.

notes: Grounds the statutory parameters for insanity defence.

query: What does Section 32 say about being forced by threats?

gold_references.label: Act to which a person is compelled by threats

required_points: Except murder and offences against the State punishable with death, acts done under compulsion of threats causing instant death apprehension are protected.
optional_points: The person must not have voluntarily placed themselves in the position of vulnerability.
forbidden_points: Claiming that compulsion or duress justifies intentional murder or execution of state treason.

query: What is the right of private defence under Section 34?

required_points: States the core foundational rule that nothing is an offence which is done in the exercise of the right of private defence.
optional_points: Serves as the gateway rule for sections 35 through 44.
forbidden_points: Stating Section 34 allows unrestricted right to strike pre-emptively without any limits.

notes: Establishes the absolute statutory baseline of private defence.

query: When does private defence of body extend to causing death?

gold_references.label: When the right of private defence of the body extends to causing death

required_points: Extends to death if the assault causes reasonable apprehension of death, grievous hurt, rape, gratifying unnatural lust, kidnapping, abduction, or wrongful confinement under circumstances of helpless rescue.
Includes throwing or administering acid or attempts to do so creating apprehension of grievous hurt.
optional_points: Subject to limitations defined in Section 37.
forbidden_points: Extending this right to cases of simple theft where no physical harm is threatened.

query: Explain abetment under Section 45.

required_points: A person abets the doing of a thing who instigates any person to do it, engages in a conspiracy to do it, or intentionally aids the doing of it.
optional_points: Explains what constitutes illegal omission or wilful misrepresentation as aid or instigation.
forbidden_points: Limiting abetment solely to physical execution of the crime.

notes: Defines parameters of multi-modal criminal abetment.

query: What is criminal conspiracy under Section 61?

required_points: When two or more persons agree to do, or cause to be done, an illegal act, or an act which is not illegal by illegal means.
An overt act is required for agreements other than an agreement to commit an offence.
optional_points: Provides the operational punishment breakdown under subsection (2).
forbidden_points: Claiming a single isolated person can commit a criminal conspiracy alone.

notes: Details statutory rules for standalone conspiracy.

query: What is rape under Section 63?

required_points: Defines rape as medical or sexual acts performed by a man on a woman under any of the seven enumerated circumstances, including against her will, without her consent, or when consent is obtained via fraud or fear.
optional_points: References the exceptions regarding medical procedures and marital status.
forbidden_points: Omitting the strict gender formulation explicitly recorded in the section text.

notes: Strict tracking of statutory text rules.

query: What is cruelty under Section 86?

gold_references.label: Cruelty by husband or relatives of husband

required_points: Cruelty means wilful conduct likely to drive a woman to suicide or cause grave injury, or harassment to coerce her or her relatives to meet unlawful dowry demands.
optional_points: Applies specifically to the husband or his relatives.
forbidden_points: Expanding this definition to protect non-domestic workplace conflicts outside the family.

notes: Statutory definitions for domestic cruelty elements.

query: What does “dishonestly” mean under BNS?

required_points: Doing anything with the intention of causing wrongful gain to one person or wrongful loss to another person.
optional_points: Relies directly on the twin concepts of wrongful gain and wrongful loss.
forbidden_points: Defining it purely as lying without a property or economic disruption element.

query: What is the meaning of wrongful gain and wrongful loss?

required_points: Wrongful gain is gain by unlawful means of property to which the person gaining is not legally entitled.
Wrongful loss is loss by unlawful means of property to which the person losing it is legally entitled.
optional_points: Includes gaining wrongfully and losing wrongfully as parts of the definition.
forbidden_points: Limiting the definition to intangible conceptual advantages not tied to property.

query: What is a document under BNS?

required_points: Any matter expressed or described upon any substance by means of letters, figures or marks, or by more than one of those means, intended to be used, or which may be used, as evidence of that matter.
Explicitly includes electronic and digital records.
optional_points: Examples are maps, inscriptions on stone, or a check endorsement.
forbidden_points: Restricting documents exclusively to physical paper formats.

query: What does counterfeit mean under BNS?

required_points: Causing one thing to resemble another thing, intending by means of that resemblance to practice deception, or knowing it to be likely that deception will thereby be practiced.
An exact imitation is not required.
optional_points: Presumption arises if the resemblance is so near that a person might be deceived.
forbidden_points: Requiring flawless structural execution for counterfeiting to occur legally.

query: What does “good faith” mean under BNS?

required_points: Nothing is said to be done or believed in 'good faith' which is done or believed without due care and attention.
optional_points: Establishes a standard of diligence rather than just pure pure motives.
forbidden_points: Defining it as internal pure intention completely isolated from negligent behavior.

query: Who is a public servant under BNS?

required_points: Enumerates various categories including commissioned officers in the Armed Forces, judges, officers of courts, every person who holds an office by virtue of which he is empowered to place or keep any person in confinement, and officers paid by the Government for public duties.
optional_points: Covers members of electoral colleges and statutory authorities.
forbidden_points: Stating private corporate employees holding no public mandate are covered.

query: What does “injury” mean under BNS?

required_points: Any harm whatever illegally caused to any person, in body, mind, reputation or property.
optional_points: Highlights the four discrete statutory dimensions of injury.
forbidden_points: Restricting 'injury' strictly to external flesh wounds or medical fractures.

query: What does “illegal” mean under BNS?

required_points: Applicable to everything which is an offence or which is prohibited by law, or which furnishes ground for a civil action.
optional_points: A person is 'legally bound to do' whatever it is illegal in them to omit.
forbidden_points: Confining 'illegal' solely to felony criminal violations.

query: What is movable property under BNS?

required_points: Intended to include corporeal property of every description, except land and things attached to the earth or permanently fastened to anything which is attached to the earth.
optional_points: Once a thing attached to the earth is severed, it becomes capable of moving and falls under this description.
forbidden_points: Classifying real estate plots or open fields as movable property.

query: What does “reason to believe” mean?

required_points: A person is said to have 'reason to believe' a thing, if he has sufficient cause to believe that thing, but not otherwise.
optional_points: Establishes a threshold higher than simple suspicion but lower than absolute empirical proof.
forbidden_points: Equating it entirely with arbitrary emotional intuition or baseless guesswork.

query: What is consent under fear or misconception?

gold_references.label: Consent known to be given under fear or misconception

required_points: Consent is not valid if given under fear of injury or misconception of fact, and the person obtaining it knows or has reason to believe it was so given.
optional_points: Also incorporates clauses regarding consent of persons of unsound mind or children under twelve years.
forbidden_points: Treating consent obtained under weapon duress as absolute and legally valid.

query: What is harbor under BNS?

required_points: Includes supplying a person with shelter, food, drink, money, clothes, arms, ammunition or means of conveyance, or assisting a person by any means to evade apprehension.
optional_points: Contains variations depending on specific exemptions like spouse rules in separate penal clauses if applicable.
forbidden_points: Limiting harbor exclusively to the physical maritime docking of transport ships.

query: What is a valuable security under BNS?

required_points: A document which is, or purports to be, a document whereby any legal right is created, extended, transferred, restricted, extinguished or released, or who acknowledges a legal liability.
optional_points: A promissory note or land deed falls directly into this category.
forbidden_points: Defining it as any casual piece of non-binding letter correspondence.

query: What is a will under BNS?

required_points: The word 'will' denotes any testamentary document.
optional_points: Applies directly across all estate forgery tracking clauses.
forbidden_points: Confusing the noun 'will' with simple psychological intent or future verbal desires.

query: What is a judge under BNS?

required_points: Denotes not only every person who is officially designated as a judge, but also every person who is empowered by law to give, in any legal proceeding, civil or criminal, a definitive judgment.
optional_points: Includes a magistrate exercising jurisdiction where decisions can result in unappealed finality.
forbidden_points: Including arbitrators or panel members who lack statutory legal decree powers.

query: What is the punishment for murder under BNS?

required_points: Mandates punishment with death or imprisonment for life, and the offender shall also be liable to a fine.
optional_points: Subsection (2) tracks specific collective mob lynching structures carrying death or life options.
forbidden_points: Allowing a simple short-term sentence like 3 years of simple custody for murder.

query: What is the punishment for theft under BNS?

required_points: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
optional_points: Provides community service alternatives for specific subsequent occurrences of low-value petty theft under 5,000 rupees if restitution is met.
forbidden_points: Stating basic simple theft carries an absolute mandatory minimum of ten years.

query: What is the punishment for cheating under BNS?

required_points: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
optional_points: Harsher aggravated terms apply under sub-sections (3) and (4) for cheating with knowledge of wrongful loss protection or delivery of property.
forbidden_points: Claiming baseline simple cheating has no imprisonment component.

query: What is the punishment for extortion under BNS?

required_points: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.
optional_points: Escalated minimums and statutory parameters apply if fear of death or grievous hurt is deployed.
forbidden_points: Stating extortion only results in a minor financial fine with zero prison exposure.

query: What is the punishment for criminal breach of trust under BNS?

gold_references.label: Punishment for criminal breach of trust

required_points: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both.
optional_points: Public servants, bankers, or agents face enhanced caps up to life or ten years under separate sub-sections.
forbidden_points: Declaring simple breach of trust cannot exceed a one year maximum sentence.

query: What is the punishment for robbery under BNS?

required_points: Rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
optional_points: If committed on the highway between sunset and sunrise, the term of rigorous imprisonment may extend to fourteen years.
forbidden_points: Omitting the mandatory requirement for rigorous status in prison calculation.

query: What is the punishment for dacoity under BNS?

required_points: Imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
optional_points: Dacoity with murder is handled separately under section 310(3) with death options.
forbidden_points: Stating that basic dacoity has a maximum term limit of three years.

query: What is the punishment for defamation under BNS?

required_points: Simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both, or with community service.
optional_points: Community service is explicit as an option in the text of the Sanhita.
forbidden_points: Prescribing rigorous hard labor as a valid choice for simple defamation.

notes: Tracks simple imprisonment and community service criteria.

query: What is the punishment for criminal trespass under BNS?

required_points: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.
optional_points: Serves as the foundation entry point for all advanced property intrusion penalties.
forbidden_points: Listing a 5-year prison sentence for a simple open-field land trespass.

query: What is the punishment for house-trespass under BNS?

required_points: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both.
optional_points: Escalates drastically if committed to perpetrate an offence punishable with death or life imprisonment.
forbidden_points: Stating simple entry into a dwelling has a structural cap of only two days.

query: What is the punishment for lurking house-trespass under BNS?

required_points: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.
optional_points: Nighttime execution pushes the penalty exposure to five years under sub-section (4).
forbidden_points: Failing to record the inclusion of fine liability along with prison terms.

query: What is the punishment for forgery under BNS?

required_points: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
optional_points: Aggravated variants like forging wills or valuable securities carry up to life sentences under subsequent clauses.
forbidden_points: Claiming basic standalone forgery initiates a mandatory ten year incarceration baseline.

query: What is the punishment for kidnapping under BNS?

required_points: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
optional_points: Ransom or murder intent escalates the situation into severe life or death categories.
forbidden_points: Applying a fine-only penalty without potential for incarceration.

query: What is the punishment for abduction under BNS?

required_points: Abduction per se is punished based on the intended purpose or crime associated with it; section 140 details kidnapping or abducting in order to murder which carries death or life sentences.
optional_points: Other sub-sections address secret confinement, extortion, or marriage exploitation intentions.
forbidden_points: Stating that simple abduction with zero criminal intent is treated as an absolute capital offence.

notes: Highlights intent dependency of abduction metrics.

query: What is the punishment for criminal intimidation under BNS?

required_points: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
optional_points: If the threat is to cause death or grievous hurt, the term may extend to seven years.
forbidden_points: Asserting that an anonymous threat letter can never exceed two years under any clause.

query: Someone pointed a knife at me and took my phone. What offence is this?

acceptable_references.label: Theft background
acceptable_references.reason: Theft is an elemental component of robbery.

required_points: This scenario constitutes Robbery under Section 309.
Theft becomes robbery because the offender causes or attempts to cause fear of instant death, hurt, or wrongful restraint.
optional_points: The presence of a knife establishes the element of immediate apprehension.
forbidden_points: Classifying it as simple theft without noting the violent coercion.

query: A man secretly takes a watch from a shop counter when the clerk isn't looking. What crime is this?

required_points: Constitutes Theft under Section 303.
Movable property is moved out of the clerk's possession dishonestly without consent.
optional_points: No force or threat was deployed, keeping it as simple theft.
forbidden_points: Labeling it extortion or robbery when zero physical fear was induced.

query: A group of six armed people enter a bank and force the cashier to hand over all the cash. What is this offence?

required_points: Constitutes Dacoity under Section 310.
When five or more persons conjointly commit or attempt to commit robbery, it is explicitly dacoity.
optional_points: Since six individuals were involved, the headcount threshold for dacoity is fully satisfied.
forbidden_points: Limiting it to a basic simple robbery charge when five or more perpetrators are engaged together.

query: A driver accidentally hits a pedestrian due to a mechanical brake failure that couldn't be foreseen. Is the driver criminally liable?

required_points: The driver is protected under the accident exception of Section 18.
The event occurred by misfortune during a lawful activity with proper care, absent any criminal intent or foresight of breakdown.
optional_points: If prior knowledge of brake mechanical failure is demonstrated, the immunity fails.
forbidden_points: Imposing strict murder liability for an unpreventable mechanical failure.

query: A person sells a fake gold chain claiming it is 24k gold and takes money for it. What offence is committed?

required_points: This constitutes Cheating under Section 318.
The buyer was fraudulently deceived into delivering cash based on a intentionally false material misrepresentation.
optional_points: Punishable under Section 318(4) because it involves delivery of property.
forbidden_points: Calling it criminal breach of trust when the dishonest intent originated prior to delivery.

query: A trustee spends the money meant for an orphanage on his own personal luxury trip. What crime is this?

required_points: Constitutes Criminal Breach of Trust under Section 316.
The individual was entrusted with property and dishonestly misappropriated it for personal use.
optional_points: Entrustment of domain over the wealth is the key distinguishing factor.
forbidden_points: Classifying it as simple external theft since possession was initially acquired lawfully via entrustment.

query: An individual signs a property deed using a prominent businessman's name to deceive the bank. What is this offence?

required_points: Constitutes Forgery under Section 336.
A false document was fabricated with intent to cause damage, injury, or practice fraud upon the bank.
optional_points: The deed represents a valuable security, exposing the perpetrator to enhanced penalty terms.
forbidden_points: Treating signature identity theft on formal instruments as simple defamation.

query: A group of five people block a public road and start damaging cars to protest. What offence is committed?

required_points: Constitutes being a member of an Unlawful Assembly (Section 189) and Rioting (Section 191).
An assembly of five or more persons executed force or violence to achieve an unlawful common object.
optional_points: Mischief is also committed concurrently via car property destruction.
forbidden_points: Exempting actions completely by calling it protected peaceful assembly when active physical vandalism is occurring.

notes: Tracks joint execution of public disorder.

query: A neighbor spreads a false rumor online that a local shopkeeper sells expired food, destroying his business reputation. What offence is this?

required_points: Constitutes Defamation under Section 356.
An imputation was published online with knowledge or reason to believe it would harm the shopkeeper's reputation.
optional_points: Electronic dissemination satisfies standard statutory publication rules.
forbidden_points: Claiming business reputational attacks are entirely exempt from criminal accountability under BNS.

query: A person threatens to publish an intimate photograph of someone unless they pay 50,000 rupees. What is this crime?

required_points: Constitutes Extortion under Section 308.
The victim was intentionally put in fear of injury to reputation/standing to compel delivery of financial property.
optional_points: The extortion mechanism relies on psychological reputational leverage rather than direct imminent physical trauma.
forbidden_points: Classifying it as simple theft when delivery is completed via active psychological duress.

query: A child of five years takes a gold ring from her mother's table and loses it in the park. Is the child guilty of an offence?

gold_references.label: Child under seven years of age

required_points: The child is completely not guilty due to Section 20.
Acts committed by anyone under seven years old cannot constitute an offence under any statutory circumstance.
optional_points: Absolute doli incapax operates as a bar here.
forbidden_points: convicting a five-year-old child for grand larceny or theft.

query: A person under the influence of involuntary intoxication (drugged by someone else) attacks a stranger. Is there criminal liability?

wrong_references.label: Unsoundness of mind
wrong_references.reason: This is a case of toxic administration, not biological systemic insanity.

required_points: The individual is exempt from liability under Section 23.
The intoxicating substance was administered entirely without knowledge or consent, rendering them incapable of understanding the nature of the act.
optional_points: The burden of proving lack of knowledge regarding administration rests on the accused during trial.
forbidden_points: Treating involuntary drugging identically to conscious voluntary drinking choices.

query: An individual enters a private backyard at 2 AM without permission to steal bicycle parts. What offence is this?

required_points: Constitutes Criminal Trespass (Section 329) and House-Trespass (Section 331).
Entry into property used as a human dwelling or its immediate curtilage was executed with intent to commit an offence (theft).
optional_points: Because it is executed at 2 AM, it triggers the aggravated classification of house-trespass by night.
forbidden_points: Calling it a simple civil fence dispute when clear intent to steal is evident.

query: A physician performs a surgical operation in good faith to save a patient's life, but the patient dies. Has an offence been committed?

gold_references.label: Act done in good faith for benefit of a person without consent

required_points: No offence was committed due to Section 26 protections.
The act was performed in good faith for the medical benefit of the patient, even if terminal results ensued.
optional_points: Aligns with core statutory medical emergency immunity illustrations.
forbidden_points: Charging the operating surgeon with intentional murder for an unsuccessful surgery.

notes: Tracks bona fide medical emergency actions.

query: A person enters a house to save a child from a fire, breaking the door down. Can the owner sue for criminal trespass?

gold_references.label: Act likely to cause harm, but done without criminal intent, and to prevent other harm

required_points: The owner cannot maintain a criminal trespass claim due to Section 19.
The act was executed without criminal intent to prevent imminent mortal destruction to a human life.
optional_points: The principle of necessity fully overrides technical property violations under these facts.
forbidden_points: Sentencing a rescuer to prison for property structural damage caused while fighting a fire.

query: How does the BNS handle offences committed by an Indian citizen outside India?

required_points: Section 1(5)(a) mandates extra-territorial jurisdiction over any citizen of India who commits an offence in any place without and beyond India.
They are triable inside India as if the act occurred within domestic borders.
optional_points: The definition of offence includes actions that would be punishable if executed locally.
forbidden_points: Claiming Indian citizens lose all criminal accountability the moment they cross international state borders.

query: If an offence is committed under the influence of voluntary vs involuntary intoxication, how does the liability change?

required_points: Involuntary intoxication (Section 23) provides absolute immunity if the substance was administered against wishes/knowledge and removes cognitive capacity.
Voluntary intoxication does not negate liability; the person is judged with the same knowledge as if they were sober.
optional_points: Specific intent patterns must still be analyzed, but voluntary choices offer no structural baseline shield.
forbidden_points: Claiming that buying and consuming alcohol voluntarily excuses felony acts entirely.

query: When does a simple theft escalate into robbery, and when does robbery become dacoity?

required_points: Theft (Section 303) escalates to Robbery (Section 309) if immediate fear of death, hurt, or restraint is introduced during execution.
Robbery escalates to Dacoity (Section 310) solely based on headcount when five or more persons conjointly commit the offence.
optional_points: Extortion can also similarly escalate into robbery under alternate clauses.
forbidden_points: Stating that dacoity requires a minimum of one hundred people to operate legally.

query: How does the definition of a public servant under Section 2 interact with punishments for bribery or public service offences?

required_points: The broad definition in Section 2(28) establishes who can be prosecuted under specific public authority corruption chapters.
Status satisfaction is mandatory before targeted public office penalty enhancements can be legally sustained.
optional_points: Covers instances of unlawful trade choices or judicial malfeasance.
forbidden_points: Prosecuting a purely private clerk under public servant specific abuse statutes.

query: What happens if a person abets a crime, but the person abetted commits a different crime instead?

gold_references.label: Liability of abettor when one act abetted and different act done

required_points: Under Section 48, the abettor is liable for the act done, in the same manner as if he had abetted it directly.
The act executed must be a probable consequence of the abetment and committed under the influence of the instigation.
optional_points: If the resulting crime is completely bizarre, unexpected, and non-consequential, liability for the final act fails.
forbidden_points: Holding an abettor automatically liable for entirely unrelated crimes outside any foreseeable vector.

notes: Tracks causal proximity rules for abetment.

query: Is life imprisonment always for whole life or can it mean fixed years?

required_points: Life imprisonment fundamentally means the remainder of natural biological life.
Section 6 sets a specific exception mapping it to twenty years strictly for computing mathematical fractions of terms.
optional_points: Executive remission powers are handled externally under procedural statutes.
forbidden_points: Stating life sentences always automatically terminate at exactly fourteen years across all situations.

query: Explain how the right of private defence is bounded by the principle of proportionality.

gold_references.label: Act against which there is no right of private defence

required_points: Section 37 explicitly mandates that the right of private defence in no case extends to the inflicting of more harm than it is necessary to inflict for the purpose of defence.
optional_points: Force deployed must correspond directly to the nature of imminent threat perceived.
forbidden_points: Sanctioning killing an unarmed fleeing child over a simple orchard fruit theft.

notes: Tracks core boundary conditions of defensive acts.

query: What is the cumulative effect of a person committing multiple distinct offences in a single incident regarding their total punishment term?

gold_references.label: Limit of punishment of offence made up of several offences

required_points: Where an act is composed of parts that are themselves separate offences, the offender shall not be punished with the punishment of more than one of such offences unless explicitly provided.
Limits aggregation where one overall crime encompasses smaller infractions.
optional_points: Prevents unconstitutional compounding of identical internal transaction entries.
forbidden_points: Adding 50 separate theft terms for 50 individual pages inside a single stolen book.

query: How do sections dealing with acts of a child change based on whether the child is under seven versus between seven and twelve?

gold_references.label: Child above seven and under twelve

required_points: Under seven (Section 20) is absolute immunity (doli incapax).
Between seven and twelve (Section 21), immunity is conditional on the child not having attained sufficient maturity of understanding to judge the nature and consequences of their conduct.
optional_points: Maturity is a fact-specific question determined by behavioral evidence at trial.
forbidden_points: Treating a entry-level conditional ten-year-old child as automatically absolutely immune without examining understanding.

notes: Tracks childhood cognitive developmental status changes.

query: If an offence is punishable with a fine only, what are the rules regarding imprisonment in default of payment of the fine?

gold_references.label: Sentence of imprisonment for non-payment of fine

required_points: If the offence is punishable with fine only, default imprisonment must be simple.
The term is strictly bounded by scale: not exceeding two months for fines up to 5,000 rupees, and four months for fines up to 10,000 rupees, maxing out at one year in other cases.
optional_points: Imprisonment terminates immediately upon payment or proportional liquidation of the fine.
forbidden_points: Ordering rigorous hard labor sentences for simple failure to pay a fine-only municipal infraction.

query: How does BNS distinguish between an act done with 'knowledge' versus an act done with 'intention' for homicide?

required_points: Intention implies a specific conscious purpose to cause death or fatal injury.
Knowledge involves structural awareness that the act is highly likely to cause death, falling into lower parameters of culpable homicide if extreme target certainty features are absent.
optional_points: Tracks the baseline distinction between basic risk awareness and active targeted execution.
forbidden_points: Treating random blind negligence identically to targeted premeditated assassination.

query: What are the provisions regarding a repeat offender under Section 13, and how does it affect punishments for theft and robbery?

gold_references.label: Enhanced punishment for certain offences after previous conviction

required_points: Section 13 mandates that whoever, having been convicted of an offence punishable under Chapter X or Chapter XVII with imprisonment of 3 years or upwards, commits a subsequent identical chapter offense faces enhanced terms up to life or ten years.
optional_points: Theft and robbery belong directly to Chapter XVII, directly invoking these recidivist escalation rules.
forbidden_points: Stating that previous convictions are completely ignored during subsequent trial sentencing.

query: If a group of persons commit a crime together, how do the concepts of joint liability or common intention apply?

gold_references.label: Acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention

query: What is the relation between criminal conspiracy and abetment by conspiracy?

required_points: Abetment by conspiracy (Section 45) requires an overt act to ensue following the agreement before prosecution manifests.
Standalone Criminal Conspiracy (Section 61) is punishable based on the agreement itself if targeted at a direct substantive offense, requiring no external overt execution.
optional_points: Both rely structurally on joint meeting of illicit intentions.
forbidden_points: Treating standalone conspiracy and abetment execution vectors as completely synonymous.

query: What is the difference between murder and culpable homicide?

required_points: Culpable homicide is the genus; murder is the specific aggravated species.
Murder requires a higher degree of probability of death and absolute certainty of intention, absent any exceptions listed under Section 101.
optional_points: All murders are culpable homicides, but not all culpable homicides constitute murder.
forbidden_points: Claiming they carry identical elements and identical punishments across all metrics.

query: What is the difference between theft and extortion?

required_points: Theft involves taking movable property secretly without consent.
Extortion involves coercing the victim into actively delivering the property via intentional induction of fear or threat.

forbidden_points: Stating theft requires weapon threats to fulfill its baseline statutory definitions.

optional_points: Restraint is partial check; confinement is total enclosure.
forbidden_points: Declaring that blocking a single highway path constitutes total cell isolation confinement.

query: What is the difference between kidnapping from India and kidnapping from lawful guardianship?

optional_points: Guardianship targets age brackets explicitly (under eighteen format blocks).

query: What is the difference between criminal trespass and house-trespass?

required_points: Criminal trespass is the general entry onto another's property with unlawful intent.
House-trespass is an aggravated form requiring intrusion into a building, tent, or vessel used as a human dwelling or place of worship.
optional_points: Structural coverage changes the baseline penalty exposure.
forbidden_points: Treating an open mountain field identically to an active private residential bedroom entry.

query: What is the difference between cheating and criminal breach of trust?

optional_points: Entrustment vs active original deception is the definitive axis.
forbidden_points: Claiming breach of trust requires active physical pickpocketing execution.

query: What is the difference between abetment and criminal conspiracy?

required_points: Abetment can be committed by a single isolated person via singular instigation or aid.
Criminal conspiracy inherently requires a minimum agreement threshold between two or more distinct minds.
optional_points: Abetment focuses on the relationship to the crime; conspiracy targets the consensus structure.
forbidden_points: Claiming a person can conspire completely alone with themselves.

query: What is the difference between criminal force and assault?

required_points: Assault is the preparation or gesture creating an apprehension that criminal force is about to be deployed.
Criminal force is the actual intentional application of physical touch or impact without consent to cause injury or fear.
optional_points: Assault is the imminent threat threat; force is the physical realization.
forbidden_points: Asserting that assault requires a complete deep entry flesh wound to exist legally.

query: What is the difference between defamation and insult?

required_points: Defamation targets objective evaluation, harming an individual's reputation in the eyes of external third parties via third party publication.
Intentional insult targets internal subjective tranquility, provoking immediate breach of peace directly between the conversing parties.
optional_points: Insult does not fundamentally depend on external third-party audience presence.
forbidden_points: Declaring that private thought processes are identical to public broadsheet print distributions.

query: What is the difference between kidnapping and abduction?

required_points: Kidnapping involves taking away a person from India or from lawful guardianship, and is minor/unsound mind centric.
Abduction involves forcing or deceitfully inducing any person (regardless of age) to move from any place.
optional_points: Kidnapping is a continuous or static substantive infraction; abduction is often auxiliary to other designs.
forbidden_points: Stating abduction only applies to children under three months of age.
